sources.title: Enhancing and Practicing Executive Function Skills with Children from Infancy to Adolescence
sources.publisher: Harvard University Center on the Developing Child
sources.type: Expert practice guide; not a trial of MIRA activities
sources.location: Printed pages 1, 6–9: introductory caveat, preschool and 5–7 activity sections
sources.access: Relevant sections read as PDF text on 2 October 2026. Not a systematic review or complete appraisal of cited research.
sources.summary: Offers age-grouped play suggestions, including movement, rhythm and sorting, as opportunities to practise attention and flexible thinking with adult support.
sources.limit: The introduction says not every suggestion is scientifically tested. No MIRA activity, safety boundary or individual benefit is validated. Older bilingual-advantage statements and competitive or physically demanding examples are not adopted.
sources.rights: Link and original bounded paraphrase only. No reproduced songs, illustrations, game text or branded materials; exact release rights review remains open.

sources.title: What Will We Make? Using Process Art to Spark Preschoolers’ Development
sources.type: Educator practice article with classroom examples
sources.location: Teaching Young Children, Winter 2023, volume 16 number 2; process art definition and introducing process art sections
sources.access: Article text, author context and copyright notice read on 2 October 2026.
sources.summary: Describes thoughtfully prepared, choice-led art exploration without a required finished product, illustrated by a classroom of four- and five-year-olds.
sources.limit: A practice account, not a controlled effectiveness study. Does not establish infant suitability, material safety or benefits of MIRA drafts. Deliberate tool scarcity and the article’s small, sharp and loose materials are not adopted.
sources.rights: Copyright 2023 NAEYC. Link and original brief paraphrase only; no copied images, dialogue or instructions. Publication rights assessment remains open.

sources.title: Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep for children under 5 years of age
sources.access: Official overview read on 2 October 2026; attempted IRIS full PDF returned an error. Full recommendations and evidence tables not appraised.
sources.summary: The guideline addresses movement, sedentary time and sleep across the day for children under five.
sources.limit: Background only: not linked as support for a draft. No activity dosage, movement prescription, five-to-six-year-old coverage or WHO endorsement is inferred.
sources.rights: Link and short original summary only; no guideline text or artwork reproduced.

claims.text: The guide proposes movement and rhythm play as practice contexts for attention and remembering actions.
claims.scope: Expert practice rationale; preschool and 5–7 sections, not exact age eligibility
claims.notSupported: A tested effect, exercise dose, required performance, safe movement prescription or suitability for a particular child.

claims.text: The guide includes comparing and sorting activities among its practice suggestions.
claims.scope: Expert practice rationale, not proof of a generated activity’s efficacy
claims.notSupported: A need to quiz, correct, race or classify children; material safety or exact developmental thresholds.

claims.text: The article describes prepared art exploration in which children choose what to make rather than copy a required product.
claims.scope: Preschool educational practice account, not a clinical or experimental finding
claims.notSupported: Guaranteed creativity, emotional interpretation of artwork, safe supplies, suitability across birth to six or approval of any MIRA draft.

primitives.name: Follow a small movement
primitives.mechanism: A child may choose a small hand movement; an adult can mirror it without asking for accuracy or a harder action.
primitives.readiness: Preschool-oriented editorial concept, not approved for any age. Reviewer must define voluntary comfortable movement, accessibility, adult availability and setting exclusions.
constraints: Only a small voluntary hand movement already chosen by the child; no prescribed position, touch, speed or range.
No standing, balance, jumping, travel, stretching, exercise, physical challenge or breathing instruction.
Adult mirrors only if invited; no correct copy, forced turn-taking, scored response or minimum duration.
Child may stop, turn away, watch or change the idea. Discomfort ends the proposal; never suggest working through it.
contexts: Child offers a small hand movement and adult follows once if invited.
Child changes their own hand movement and decides whether the adult joins again.

primitives.name: Share an invented rhythm
primitives.mechanism: An adult can echo a child’s voluntary quiet vocal rhythm, leaving the child free to repeat, change or leave it.
materials: Voices only; no recording, instrument or props
primitives.readiness: Preschool-oriented editorial concept. Vocal comfort, sound sensitivity, support and age applicability need independent review; silence is not inability.
constraints: Use a quiet spontaneous sound only; no named song, lyrics, melody transcription or imposed words.
No required volume, pitch, length, breath control or matching accuracy.
No touching, tapping bodies, clapping near ears or adding objects.
Child chooses whether to take part and can turn away or stop; adult must not insist or increase volume.
contexts: Adult responds briefly to a quiet rhythm the child has just offered.
Child alters a rhythm they initiated and adult leaves room rather than correcting it.

primitives.name: Explore marks without a model
primitives.mechanism: With an independently reviewed material set, the child can choose marks and decide whether to describe or change them; the adult need not set an end product.
materials: Plain drawing paper and an age-labelled intact crayon; exact product, dimensions, condition and suitability remain unapproved
primitives.readiness: Preschool-oriented editorial concept only. Material ingestion/mouthing, breakage, grip/access needs and surface/supervision requirements must be resolved before release. Not infant art advice.
constraints: Mention paper and crayon only; no paint, glue, cutting, small loose parts, water, recycled items or substitutions.
Never call the supplies safe or approved. Full material and supervision review is still required.
Do not supply a picture to copy, correct grip, demand a finished drawing, label emotions or infer meaning from marks.
No hand-over-hand assistance. Child may decline, watch, leave marks unfinished or stop.
contexts: Child chooses whether to make marks on plain paper without an adult model.
Child chooses whether to revisit their own marks, add something or leave them as they are.

primitives.name: Try an arrangement
primitives.mechanism: A child can arrange a reviewed set of large play blocks in their own way and change the arrangement without needing to name a rule.
materials: Large intact lightweight play blocks with no detachable parts; exact set, dimensions and condition await review
primitives.readiness: Preschool-oriented editorial concept only. Reviewer must establish object safety, access, surface, supervision and age boundaries; generic large/lightweight descriptions are insufficient.
constraints: Blocks stay in a single layer on an already reviewed surface; no stacks, throwing, containers or other objects.
No required colour/shape knowledge, right answer, timed sorting, counting target or testing question.
Adult follows a child-chosen arrangement; help is available, never withheld to make a challenge.
Child can stop, redirect, watch or leave the arrangement. No forced cleanup as a completion condition.
contexts: Child chooses an arrangement of the reviewed blocks and may invite the adult to join.
Child changes their own arrangement while the adult leaves the choice open.
